stem: What is the width of the paper, in yards?
stimulus: A printmaker orders a roll of heavyweight paper for pulling large woodcut prints. The roll is 54 inches wide.
explanation: This question gives you a measurement in one unit and asks for it in another. There is no rate and no story to model. You need the standard factor 1 yard = 36 inches (3 feet per yard × 12 inches per foot). Write the conversion fraction with inches on the bottom so that inches cancel: $54 \text{ in} \times \dfrac{1 \text{ yd}}{36 \text{ in}} = \dfrac{54}{36} \text{ yd} = 1.5 \text{ yd}$. Check the direction: a yard is bigger than an inch, so the number of yards has to be smaller than 54. It is. If you prefer to chain through feet, do $54 \text{ in} \times \dfrac{1 \text{ ft}}{12 \text{ in}} \times \dfrac{1 \text{ yd}}{3 \text{ ft}} = 1.5 \text{ yd}$. Don't stop after the first factor.

common_errors.why: Multiplied 54 by 36 instead of dividing. That converts the wrong way and makes the yard count larger than the inch count.
Divided 54 by 12 to get feet and stopped there, without the second factor that converts feet to yards.
Used the wrong standard factor from memory, 3 inches per yard (mixing it up with 3 feet per yard), and computed 54 ÷ 3.
Used 12 inches per yard instead of 36 and computed 54 ÷ 12. This gives the same value as stopping at feet.

stem: How many gallons of water does the tank hold when it is full?
stimulus: A hydrologist stores groundwater samples in a holding tank with a volume of 77 cubic feet. One gallon is equal to 231 cubic inches.
explanation: This is a straight conversion from cubic feet to gallons. The question gives you the gallon in cubic inches, so you chain through cubic inches. First you need the cubic factor. Since 1 foot = 12 inches, 1 cubic foot = $12 \times 12 \times 12 = 1{,}728$ cubic inches, not 12. Then set up the chain so that each unwanted unit cancels: $77 \text{ ft}^3 \times \dfrac{1{,}728 \text{ in}^3}{1 \text{ ft}^3} \times \dfrac{1 \text{ gal}}{231 \text{ in}^3}$. Simplify before you multiply: $\dfrac{77}{231} = \dfrac{1}{3}$, so the result is $\dfrac{1{,}728}{3} = 576$ gallons. Check the direction: a gallon is smaller than a cubic foot, so the number of gallons should be larger than 77. It is.

common_errors.why: Used the linear factor 12 inches per foot instead of the cubic factor 1,728 cubic inches per cubic foot: 77 × 12 ÷ 231 = 4.
Used the square factor 144 instead of the cubic factor 1,728: 77 × 144 ÷ 231 = 48.
Converted to cubic inches (77 × 1,728) and stopped there, without dividing by 231 to get gallons.
Flipped both conversion fractions, computing 77 × 231 ÷ 1,728 ≈ 10.29. That converts the wrong way at each step.
Divided 77 by 231 and forgot to multiply by the cubic-inch factor at all.

stem: A labour economist studying unpaid overtime found that one employee worked a total of 7,200 minutes of unrecorded overtime in a year. The economist reports overtime in standard workdays, where 1 workday is 8 hours. How many workdays is 7,200 minutes equivalent to?
explanation: Write the amount with its unit, then multiply by fractions equal to 1 so that each unit you don't want cancels. First change minutes to hours, which you know: $7{,}200 \text{ min} \times \frac{1 \text{ hr}}{60 \text{ min}} = 120 \text{ hr}$. Then change hours to workdays using the factor given: $120 \text{ hr} \times \frac{1 \text{ workday}}{8 \text{ hr}} = 15 \text{ workdays}$. As one chain, that is $7{,}200 \times \frac{1}{60} \times \frac{1}{8} = 15$. Check the direction: a workday is a much larger unit than a minute, so the number should get much smaller, and it does.

common_errors.why: You changed minutes to hours and stopped there, so you never used the 8-hour workday.
You got 120 hours correctly, then multiplied by 8 instead of dividing. That converts the wrong way, as if a workday were smaller than an hour.
You divided 7,200 by 8 straight away and skipped the minutes-to-hours step, so you treated minutes as if they were hours.
You used a 24-hour calendar day ($120 \div 24$) in place of the stated 8-hour workday.

stem: A printmaker carves an image into a rectangular linoleum block with an area of 2.25 square feet. What is the area of the block, in square inches?
explanation: There are 12 inches in 1 foot. Square units hold one unit in each of two directions, so you need the conversion factor twice: $2.25 \text{ ft}^2 \times \frac{12 \text{ in}}{1 \text{ ft}} \times \frac{12 \text{ in}}{1 \text{ ft}} = 2.25 \times 144 \text{ in}^2 = 324 \text{ in}^2$. Check that the units cancel: both factors of ft cancel against $\text{ft}^2$ and leave $\text{in}^2$. Check the direction: an inch is smaller than a foot, so the number should get bigger.

common_errors.why: You multiplied by 12 only once, so one ft is left uncancelled. You found $\text{in}\cdot\text{ft}$, not square inches.
You divided by 144 instead of multiplying, which converts the wrong way. Going to a smaller unit must give a larger number. (Truncated value of $2.25/144 = 0.015625$.)
You divided by 12 just once, so you made both mistakes: the conversion goes the wrong way and is missing its second factor.
You applied the square to the 2.25 and the 12 together, as if the area were $(2.25 \cdot 12)^2/9$ or $(1.5 \cdot 6)^2$. Writing out the cancelling factors avoids this slip.

stem: How many fluid ounces of hand sanitizer is this? (1 gallon = 4 quarts and 1 quart = 32 fluid ounces)
stimulus: A county health department sets aside 2.5 gallons of hand sanitizer for a weekend vaccination clinic.
explanation: Write the amount with its unit, then multiply by conversion fractions that cancel the units you don't want. Put the old unit in the denominator each time: $2.5\text{ gal} \times \frac{4\text{ qt}}{1\text{ gal}} \times \frac{32\text{ fl oz}}{1\text{ qt}}$. Gallons cancel, then quarts cancel, and fluid ounces are left. The arithmetic is $2.5 \times 4 = 10$, then $10 \times 32 = 320$. Check the direction: fluid ounces are much smaller than gallons, so the number should get much bigger, and it does.

common_errors.why: Converted gallons to quarts and stopped there, one factor short of the two-step chain.
Multiplied 2.5 by 32 directly and dropped the gallons-to-quarts factor of 4.
Multiplied by 4 but then divided by 32 instead of multiplying, so the second factor went the wrong way: $2.5 \times 4 \div 32$.

stem: How many yards is this altitude? (1 mile = 5,280 feet)
stimulus: A weather balloon released by a meteorologist to measure upper-air temperatures reached an altitude of 4.5 miles before it burst.
explanation: Chain through feet. Start with $4.5\text{ mi} \times \frac{5280\text{ ft}}{1\text{ mi}}$, which cancels miles and gives $23{,}760$ feet. Then multiply by $\frac{1\text{ yd}}{3\text{ ft}}$ so that feet cancel: $23{,}760 \div 3 = 7{,}920$ yards. Check the direction: a yard is longer than a foot, so the yard count should be smaller than the foot count.

common_errors.why: Converted miles to feet and gave that as the answer without the feet-to-yards step.
Multiplied the feet by 3 instead of dividing, so the second conversion went the wrong way.
Divided 4.5 by 3 as if the given value were already in feet, and ignored the 5,280 factor.

stem: How many seconds of music does the collection contain?
stimulus: A musicologist cataloguing a collection of Baroque harpsichord recordings finds that the recordings run 2.25 hours in total.
explanation: Use the standard factors 60 minutes per hour and 60 seconds per minute: $2.25\text{ h} \times \frac{60\text{ min}}{1\text{ h}} \times \frac{60\text{ s}}{1\text{ min}}$. Hours cancel, then minutes cancel. $2.25 \times 60 = 135$ minutes, and $135 \times 60 = 8{,}100$ seconds. Note that 2.25 hours means two and a quarter hours. It does not mean 2 hours 25 minutes.

common_errors.why: Converted hours to minutes and stopped before converting minutes to seconds.
Read 2.25 hours as 2 hours 25 minutes, which gives 145 minutes and then 8,700 seconds.
Divided by 60 twice instead of multiplying, so the conversion went the wrong way: $2.25 \div 3600$.

stem: What is the length of the boot, in yards?
stimulus: In a folktale collected by a folklore scholar, a giant's boot is said to be 3 ells long. The scholar notes that the ell used in the region where the tale was collected equals 45 inches.
explanation: Chain through inches. $3\text{ ells} \times \frac{45\text{ in}}{1\text{ ell}} = 135$ inches. A yard is 36 inches, so multiply by $\frac{1\text{ yd}}{36\text{ in}}$: $135 \div 36 = 3.75$ yards. Check the direction: a yard is longer than an inch, so the count should drop sharply from 135.

common_errors.why: Converted ells to inches and stopped without converting inches to yards.
Used 12 inches per yard (which is inches per foot) and divided 135 by 12.
Multiplied 135 by 36 instead of dividing, so the second conversion went the wrong way.

stem: How many inches below the surface is the holdfast?
stimulus: A marine biologist surveying a kelp forest records that one kelp holdfast is anchored 2.5 fathoms below the water's surface. A fathom is 6 feet.
explanation: Chain through feet. $2.5\text{ fathoms} \times \frac{6\text{ ft}}{1\text{ fathom}} = 15$ feet. Then multiply by $\frac{12\text{ in}}{1\text{ ft}}$: $15 \times 12 = 180$ inches. Check the direction: inches are smaller than feet, so the number should grow.

common_errors.why: Converted fathoms to feet and stopped before converting to inches.
Divided 15 feet by 12 instead of multiplying, so the second conversion went the wrong way.
Used 3 inches per foot instead of 12 and multiplied 15 by 3.

stem: A paleobotanist measures a fossil fern frond preserved in shale and records its length as 4.5 inches. Given that 1 inch equals 2.54 centimeters, what is the length of the frond, in millimeters?
explanation: Write the length with its unit, then multiply by conversion fractions so each unwanted unit cancels. Put the old unit in the denominator each time: $4.5 \text{ in} \times \frac{2.54 \text{ cm}}{1 \text{ in}} \times \frac{10 \text{ mm}}{1 \text{ cm}}$. Inches cancel, then centimeters cancel, and only millimeters are left. The arithmetic is $4.5 \times 2.54 = 11.43$, and $11.43 \times 10 = 114.3$. Check the direction: millimeters are much smaller than inches, so the number should get much bigger, and it does.

common_errors.why: Converted inches to centimeters and stopped, leaving out the second factor that turns centimeters into millimeters.
Got 11.43 cm, then divided by 10 instead of multiplying when going from centimeters to the smaller unit, millimeters.
Divided 4.5 by 2.54 instead of multiplying, which gives about 1.772, then multiplied by 10 correctly to get 17.72.

stem: A weather station's snow stake shows that 1.5 yards of snow accumulated on the ground over one winter. What is this depth, in inches?
explanation: You need standard factors here: 1 yard = 3 feet and 1 foot = 12 inches. Chain them so yards and then feet cancel: $1.5 \text{ yd} \times \frac{3 \text{ ft}}{1 \text{ yd}} \times \frac{12 \text{ in}}{1 \text{ ft}} = 1.5 \times 36 = 54$ inches. Inches are smaller than yards, so the answer should be larger than 1.5, and it is.

common_errors.why: Converted yards to feet ($1.5 \times 3$) and stopped before converting feet to inches.
Remembered the factor wrong, using 12 inches per yard instead of 36, so computed $1.5 \times 12$.
Divided by 36 instead of multiplying ($1.5 \div 36$), which converts the wrong way.

stem: A complete concert performance of a cycle of piano sonatas lasts 2.4 hours. How many seconds long is the performance?
explanation: Chain two factors through minutes: $2.4 \text{ h} \times \frac{60 \text{ min}}{1 \text{ h}} \times \frac{60 \text{ s}}{1 \text{ min}}$. Hours cancel, then minutes cancel. The arithmetic is $2.4 \times 60 = 144$ minutes, and $144 \times 60 = 8640$ seconds. Seconds are much smaller than hours, so a large number makes sense.

common_errors.why: Converted hours to minutes and stopped before converting minutes to seconds.
Divided 2.4 by 60 instead of multiplying, which converts toward a larger unit instead of a smaller one.
Treated 2.4 hours as 2 hours 40 minutes ($2 \times 60 + 40 = 160$... or read the decimal as 100 minutes per hour, $2.4 \times 100 = 240$), using a decimal place-value factor instead of 60.

stem: In a historical textile ledger, cloth is measured in ells, where 1 ell is equal to 45 inches. A bolt of wool is recorded as 16 ells long. What is the length of this bolt, in yards?
explanation: Chain through inches, because inches link the two units: $16 \text{ ells} \times \frac{45 \text{ in}}{1 \text{ ell}} \times \frac{1 \text{ yd}}{36 \text{ in}}$. Ells cancel, then inches cancel. The arithmetic is $16 \times 45 = 720$ inches, and $720 \div 36 = 20$ yards. An ell (45 in) is longer than a yard (36 in), so the number of yards should be a little more than 16, and it is.

common_errors.why: Converted ells to inches and stopped before converting inches to yards.
Divided 720 inches by 12, which gives the length in feet instead of yards.
Flipped the conversion, computing $16 \times \frac{36}{45}$, so the inches-per-ell and inches-per-yard factors are used the wrong way round.
